natural: Late August on the plateau. Thirty-one degrees forecast, the south blinds already down, and three months after go-live the fourth floor still smells of new carpet.
plain: It is late August in Kirchberg. The forecast is 31 degrees. The blinds on the south side are already closed. The new lending platform went live three months ago. The fourth floor still smells of new carpet.

natural: Marie Curie runs Reporting now. Two screens, eleven windows open across them, and beside the keyboard a printed page with pencil on it.
plain: Marie Curie is now Head of Reporting. She has two screens with eleven windows open. Next to her keyboard there is a printed page with pencil marks on it.

natural: You are early. Sit there. Second-quarter exposure pack. It went to the Board on Friday and nobody has complained, which is the only review it gets.
plain: You are early. Sit here. This is the exposure pack for the second quarter. It went to the Board of Directors on Friday. Nobody has complained, and that is the only review it receives.

natural: It looks finished.
plain: It looks finished.

natural: It is finished. I want you to see what finishing it costs. Eleven files. Four people. Five working days. Every quarter.
plain: It is finished. I want you to see what it costs to finish it. Eleven files. Four people. Five working days. Every three months.

natural: The platform holds all of it.
plain: The lending platform already holds all of that data.

natural: The platform holds all of it. The Board cannot see the platform. Risk cannot see the platform. A supervisor in Vilnius most certainly cannot see the platform.
plain: The platform holds all of it. But the Board of Directors cannot see the platform. The Risk division cannot see it. A national supervisor in Vilnius certainly cannot see it.

natural: Grace Hopper arrives with two coffees and puts one down on the printed page without looking.
plain: Grace Hopper arrives with two coffees. She puts one down on the printed page without looking.

natural: Tab six is mine. I send her the maturity buckets by mail on the Tuesday and she pastes them in. That is the state of the art in this building.
plain: Tab six is my work. I send Marie the maturity figures by e-mail on the Tuesday and she copies them into the file. That is our current method.

natural: Tab six is the one Internal Audit named. Twice. Which copy is current, and who changed it, and when.
plain: Tab six is the one the internal auditors wrote about. Twice. Their questions are: which copy is the current one, who changed it, and when.

natural: So build the report.
plain: So build the report.

natural: Which one?
plain: Which report?

natural: The exposure report.
plain: The exposure report.

natural: There is no exposure report. There are three. The Board wants one page. Risk wants stress scenarios on it. Finance wants every figure reconciled to the accounts.
plain: There is no single exposure report. There are three. The Board wants one page. The Risk division wants stress scenarios included. The Finance division wants every figure checked against the accounts.

natural: And it moves. In April Risk wanted the scenarios weighted. In July they wanted them unweighted and split by maturity. In October it will be something else and they will be right both times.
plain: And it changes. In April, Risk wanted the scenarios weighted. In July, they wanted them unweighted and split by maturity. In October it will be something else, and they will be right on both occasions.

natural: Then somebody writes a specification and we argue about it until March.
plain: Then somebody writes a specification and we argue about it until March.

natural: We did that. Two hundred and twelve requirements, and it worked, because every person in the room already knew what a disbursement was.
plain: We did that on the last project. We wrote 212 requirements and it worked. It worked because everyone in the room already knew what a disbursement was.

natural: Ask Risk to specify this and they will describe a screen. They will describe the screen they have imagined, and we will build it, and it will be wrong by the second quarter.
plain: If you ask Risk to write the specification, they will describe a screen. They will describe the screen they have imagined. We will build it, and by the second quarter it will be wrong.

natural: Marie. If the Board asked you this morning what the report should contain, what would you send them?
plain: Marie, if the Board asked you this morning what the report should contain, what would you send them?

natural: Mine. Grace would send hers. Both would be defensible and they would not match.
plain: I would send my version. Grace would send hers. Both would be defensible, and the two would not match.

natural: I have Florence at eleven and I have no number for her. I know what it costs us. I do not know what it costs to stop.
plain: I meet Florence Nightingale at 11:00 and I have no figure for her. I know what the current situation costs us. I do not know what it would cost to fix it.

natural: Start with the thing nobody has written down. Not the screens. The problem. Four analysts, five days, eleven files, and three people who want three different reports.
plain: Start with the thing nobody has written down. Not the screens. The problem. Four analysts, five days, eleven files, and three people who want three different reports.

natural: Two of my four did this in 2027 as well, before the platform. The numbers got cleaner. The five days did not move.
plain: Two of my four analysts did this work in 2027 too, before the new platform existed. The numbers became cleaner. The five days did not change.

natural: No project. No budget, no charter, no team. A printed page with pencil on it, a coffee ring now drying on the corner of it, and a problem nobody has yet agreed on.
plain: There is no project. No budget, no charter, no team. There is a printed page with pencil marks, a drying coffee ring on one corner, and a problem that nobody has yet agreed on.

natural: Lorenzo de' Medici keeps a shelf of finished things. The CASTOR Project-End Report is on it, spine out. On the desk, one page: a Project Initiation Request dated today.
plain: Lorenzo de' Medici keeps a shelf of completed projects. The CASTOR Project-End Report stands on it. On the desk there is a single page: a Project Initiation Request dated today.

natural: Two and a half years ago Grace sat in that chair and told me precisely what eight point four million would buy. It bought it. Six weeks late, and it bought it.
plain: Two and a half years ago, Grace sat in that chair and told me exactly what 8.4 million euro would buy. It bought that. It was six weeks late, but it bought it.

natural: Now read me the third line of this one.
plain: Now read me the third line of this page.

natural: The content of the report cannot be specified in advance.
plain: 'The content of the report cannot be specified in advance.'

natural: Yes. So what am I funding?
plain: Yes. So what am I paying for?

natural: The portal.
plain: The portal.

natural: Florence, you cannot tell me what is on it.
plain: Florence, you cannot tell me what will be on it.

natural: Not in September 2028. No.
plain: Not in September 2028. No, we cannot.

natural: Then that is an argument for waiting, not for spending. Talk me out of it.
plain: Then that is a reason to wait, not a reason to spend money. Persuade me otherwise.

natural: Waiting does not make it knowable. Risk changes the question every quarter because their mandate changes every quarter. In a year you buy the same uncertainty at 2029 prices.
plain: Waiting will not make it knowable. The Risk division changes the question every quarter, because their work changes every quarter. If you wait a year, you buy the same uncertainty at 2029 prices.

natural: And my division writes a specification that four people sign and none of them believe. I have done that. It is expensive and it is quiet.
plain: And my division would write a specification that four people sign and nobody believes. I have done that before. It is expensive, and nobody complains until much later.

natural: This is the part where somebody tells me agile is faster.
plain: This is the moment where somebody usually tells me that agile is faster.

natural: It is not faster. It plans more than CASTOR did, and more often, and by more people. That is the actual difference and it is not a selling point.
plain: It is not faster. It involves more planning than CASTOR did, more often, and by more people. That is the real difference, and it is not a sales argument.

natural: Then what do I lose?
plain: Then what do I lose?

natural: Nothing you had. Business Case. Charter. Architecture Overview and Operational Model, because there is an information system in it. Four phases, the same gates, this board at the top of them.
plain: Nothing that you had before. A Business Case. A Project Charter. An Architecture Overview and an Operational Model, because the solution contains an information system. Four phases, the same gates, and this board above them.

natural: And what do I gain that CASTOR could not give me?
plain: And what do I gain that CASTOR could not give me?

natural: Four decisions instead of one. Four releases in 2029, each usable. You can stop after the second and keep the first two.
plain: Four decisions instead of one. Four releases during 2029, each one usable. You can stop after the second release and still keep what the first two delivered.

natural: You could not do that with a platform. With a platform you find out in month twenty-two.
plain: You could not do that when buying a platform. With a platform you find out in month twenty-two.

natural: And what leaves the portfolio to make room for it?
plain: And what leaves the investment portfolio to make room for it?

natural: The reporting warehouse refresh. It has slipped every year since 2026 and its business case is this one, written worse.
plain: The reporting warehouse refresh. It has been delayed every year since 2026, and its business case is the same as this one, written badly.

natural: I have been waiting four years for somebody to say that out loud. Grace. You still owe me a number on the last one.
plain: I have waited four years for somebody to say that out loud. Grace, you still owe me a figure on the previous project.

natural: Full-year 2029, to this board, February 2030. Four of five criteria met on the day we closed, one of them still a blank line. It has not changed.
plain: The full-year figures for 2029 come to this board in February 2030. On the day we closed, four of the five success criteria were met and one was still empty. That has not changed.

natural: One more, then I have the Governors at five. If it is agile, and the team organises itself, who exactly do I shout at?
plain: One more question, then I meet the Governors at 17:00. If this is agile, and the team organises its own work, who exactly do I hold responsible?

natural: Me. That part does not move.
plain: Me. That part does not change.

natural: Good. Then one sentence, and I will sign the page. What am I buying?
plain: Good. Then give me one sentence and I will sign the page. What am I buying?

natural: So I am buying the same controls and a different construction method. That I can defend. Bring me a Business Case by October and do not make it long.
plain: So I am buying the same controls with a different way of building. I can defend that. Bring me a Business Case in October, and keep it short.

natural: CASTOR took two years because it replaced a payments system. This one is smaller. That is not the same claim and he will notice.
plain: CASTOR took two years because it replaced a payments system. This project is smaller. That is a different claim, and he will notice.

natural: Fix it with whom? Risk changed the scenario basis twice this year. You would be buying a specification with a shelf life of one quarter.
plain: Agree it with whom? Risk changed the basis of the scenarios twice this year. You would be buying a specification that is out of date after one quarter.

natural: He did not complain about the paperwork. He complained about paying for a decision he could not revisit. Do not fix the wrong grievance.
plain: He did not complain about the paperwork. He complained about paying for a decision he could not change later. Do not solve the wrong problem.

natural: B4-12 has been repainted and the video kit is the same video kit. Grace Hopper has two windows open: a blank Business Case, and the CASTOR one from 2026, for the section numbers.
plain: Room B4-12 has been repainted. The video equipment is the same one. Grace Hopper has two windows open: an empty Business Case, and the CASTOR Business Case from 2026, to copy the section numbers.

natural: Same template. Section for section. I went looking for the agile version and there is not one.
plain: It is the same template, section by section. I looked for an agile version and there is no such thing.

natural: There is not one. Business Case, Project Charter, Architecture Overview, Operational Model. All four, because there is an information system in the solution.
plain: There is no agile version. Business Case, Project Charter, Architecture Overview, Operational Model. All four are required, because the solution contains an information system.

natural: Four point six million. Eighteen months. Eighteen hundred and fifty person-days. In-house team, two seconded from Levallois.
plain: 4.6 million euro. Eighteen months. 1,850 person-days. An in-house team, with two people seconded from Levallois Systems.

natural: And an alternatives section that will disappoint everybody. Do nothing. Extend the platform's reporting screens. Build a portal. We recommend the portal.
plain: And a section on alternatives that will disappoint everyone. Do nothing. Extend the reporting screens of the existing platform. Build a portal. We recommend the portal.

natural: Read me the second criterion.
plain: Read me the second success criterion.

natural: Time to deliver a new report view. Baseline about one quarter. Target one iteration, two weeks.
plain: Time to deliver a new report view. The current figure is about one quarter. The target is one iteration, which is two weeks.

natural: Keep it there and keep the number. That criterion is the entire argument for doing it this way. Take it out and by March we are a slow portal project.
plain: Keep that criterion, with the number. That criterion is the whole reason for working this way. If you remove it, by March we are just a slow portal project.

natural: SC1 is the one I get asked about at dinner. Five days and four analysts, down to one day and one analyst. And SC3, eleven spreadsheets to zero.
plain: The first criterion is the one people ask me about socially. Five days and four analysts, down to one day and one analyst. And the third criterion: eleven spreadsheets down to zero.

natural: Zero is a hard number to be wrong about. I would rather have five criteria we can count than nine we can argue about.
plain: Zero is a number you cannot be vague about. I would prefer five criteria we can count to nine we can argue about.

natural: Five is what we did last time. Four met, one blank, and I am still measuring the blank one for Lorenzo in 2030.
plain: Five is what we used last time. Four were met, one was left empty, and I am still measuring that one for Lorenzo until 2030.

natural: Section 3.5 goes up on the screen. Four features and nothing else: member-state exposure, instrument and maturity views, scenario overlay and national-authority access, self-service report builder.
plain: Section 3.5 appears on the screen. It contains four features and nothing else: exposure by member state, instrument and maturity views, scenario overlay with national-authority access, and a self-service report builder.

natural: Four. And the fourth one is in there because Risk changes its question every quarter, and I would rather they answered their own.
plain: Four features. The fourth one is there because the Risk division changes its question every quarter, and I would prefer them to answer it themselves.

natural: Those four give me maybe sixty stories. Marie writes them, not this document.
plain: Those four features will produce about sixty stories. Marie writes those stories, not this document.

natural: Section 5.1. Say the word out loud so it is minuted.
plain: Section 5.1. Say the word out loud so that it appears in the minutes.

natural: PM²-Agile. Phases unchanged, gates unchanged, governance unchanged. Executing in two-week iterations.
plain: PM²-Agile. The phases do not change, the gates do not change, the governance does not change. The Executing phase runs in two-week iterations.

natural: And section six. There is a box on my organigram that says A-PCT and I do not know what goes in it.
plain: And section six. There is a box on my organisation chart that says A-PCT, and I do not know who belongs in it.

natural: Marie, Ada, Einstein, three developers. Grace stays where she is. So do I.
plain: Marie, Ada, Einstein and three developers. Grace keeps her role. So do I.

natural: Twelve October at the Corporate Investment Board. Both documents, one meeting. Lorenzo has forty minutes and eleven items.
plain: On 12 October at the Corporate Investment Board. Both documents, in one meeting. Lorenzo has forty minutes and eleven agenda items.

natural: Nightingale writes a date on the back of her hand, which is the only planning tool in the room that has never once failed her.
plain: Nightingale writes a date on the back of her hand. It is the only planning tool in the room that has never failed her.

natural: Who signs which document? I ask because I file them.
plain: Who signs which document? I ask because I am the one who files them.

natural: Grace writes the Business Case, Florence is accountable for it. I complete the Charter and submit it, and this committee is accountable for that one.
plain: Grace writes the Business Case and Florence is accountable for it. I complete the Project Charter and submit it, and the Steering Committee is accountable for that one.

natural: I have all the numbers open in front of me. Give me two days and I will write the Charter as well.
plain: I have all the figures open in front of me. Give me two days and I will write the Project Charter too.

natural: Fine. I will start section three and you can be responsible for it at half past four. Florence, you are consulted. That is a demotion from the Business Case and I want it noted.
plain: All right. I will start section three, and it becomes your responsibility at 16:30. Florence, you are only consulted here. That is less than on the Business Case, and I want that recorded.

natural: I am responsible for two things and neither of them is this. The handbook and the work plan. Do not put me on a row I am not on.
plain: I am responsible for two documents, and this is not one of them. The Development Handbook and the Development Work Plan. Do not put me in a row where I do not belong.

natural: The features are yours and the stories are mine. If I write both, nobody can tell me later that I have drifted from the charter.
plain: The features belong to your document and the stories belong to mine. If I wrote both, nobody could later show me that I had drifted away from the charter.

natural: Then there is no baseline. In fourteen months somebody asks what we said we would build, and the answer is a list that has been re-sorted eighty times.
plain: Then there is no baseline. In fourteen months somebody will ask what we said we would build, and the only answer is a list that has been reordered eighty times.

natural: On the twelfth the Corporate Investment Board approved the Business Case and gave corporate approval to the Charter. In the same minute the reporting warehouse refresh left the portfolio, after four years of not being cancelled.
plain: On 12 October the Corporate Investment Board approved the Business Case and gave corporate approval of the Charter. In the same minute the reporting warehouse refresh was removed from the portfolio, after four years of not being cancelled.

natural: I did not book this room. The secretariat did, and I want it on record that I assumed there would not be a gate, because the project is agile.
plain: I did not book this room. The secretariat did. I want it recorded that I assumed there would be no gate, because the project is agile.

natural: That sentence is going to do a great deal of work over the next eighteen months.
plain: That sentence will be used to explain many things over the next eighteen months.

natural: Four phases. Initiating, Planning, Executing, Closing. Same four, same order, same gates between them. What is iterative is what happens inside Executing.
plain: There are four phases: Initiating, Planning, Executing, Closing. The same four, in the same order, with the same gates between them. Only the work inside Executing is iterative.

natural: Serial in the large, iterative in the small. It is a slogan, and it is also literally the plan.
plain: Serial in the large, iterative in the small. It is a slogan, and it is also exactly the plan.

natural: Same sheet as last time. Initiating tab. Twenty-eight questions, and the Project Manager answers all of them before asking this committee for anything.
plain: It is the same sheet as last time. The Initiating tab. Twenty-eight questions. The Project Manager answers all of them before asking this committee for anything.

natural: And the answers.
plain: And what are the answers?

natural: Twenty-six clean. Two partial. The Architecture Overview exists at version zero point four, which is what Initiating asks for and not a page more. And Eiffel's secondment is agreed and unsigned.
plain: Twenty-six are clear. Two are partial. The Architecture Overview exists at version 0.4, which is what the Initiating phase requires and nothing more. And Gustave Eiffel's secondment is agreed but not yet signed.

natural: An architecture document, in Initiating? Last time I saw nothing of the sort until June.
plain: An architecture document, in the Initiating phase? Last time I saw nothing like that until June.

natural: On the last project there was no such artefact. Architecture Overview and Operational Model are created in Initiating, then updated in Planning and Executing. Governance, not design.
plain: On the last project that document did not exist. The Architecture Overview and the Operational Model are created in Initiating, then updated in Planning and Executing. They are governance documents, not detailed designs.

natural: So what is actually different? I have been in three meetings and it looks like the last project with new stationery.
plain: So what is actually different? I have attended three meetings and it looks like the last project with new stationery.

natural: What happens after the second gate.
plain: What happens after the second gate is different.

natural: And the people. Say the roles, Henry needs them for the organigram.
plain: And the people are different. Say the roles out loud. Henry needs them for the organisation chart.

natural: Team Coordinator. I facilitate, I coach, I remove obstacles, and I keep project management away from the team so they can build.
plain: I am the Team Coordinator. I facilitate, I coach and I remove obstacles. I keep project management concerns away from the team so that they can build.

natural: So, a Scrum Master.
plain: So, a Scrum Master.

natural: No. And do not translate the rest of it either. Scrum covers construction. This has to cover a lifecycle with your gates in it.
plain: No. And do not translate the other words either. Scrum covers the construction work. This has to cover a whole lifecycle, including your gates.

natural: Product Owner. I hold the list of what gets built and the order it gets built in. Continuously, not quarterly.
plain: I am the Product Owner. I hold the list of what will be built and the order in which it will be built. I do that continuously, not once a quarter.

natural: And I am still the Business Manager, which until last week I thought meant I decided that.
plain: And I am still the Business Manager. Until last week I thought that meant I decided those things.

natural: You represent Florence. I take the daily decisions. If those two ever point in different directions we have a real problem and not a paperwork one.
plain: You represent Florence. I take the day-to-day decisions. If those two ever point in different directions, we have a real problem and not a paperwork problem.

natural: Note the date, Henry. I want to know how long that lasts.
plain: Write the date down, Henry. I want to know how long that arrangement lasts.

natural: Third one. Albert Einstein, Architecture Owner, seconded from Enterprise Architecture. He starts Monday and he has already sent me four questions.
plain: The third role is Architecture Owner. Albert Einstein, seconded from Enterprise Architecture. He starts on Monday and he has already sent me four questions.

natural: Nobody approves this checklist, incidentally. I assure the answers. The committee authorises the phase. Those are three different acts and people confuse them every time.
plain: Nobody approves this checklist, by the way. I check the answers as quality assurance. The committee authorises the change of phase. Those are three separate actions and people confuse them every time.

natural: Then authorise it and give me the next date.
plain: Then let us authorise it. Give me the next date.

natural: Twenty-third. First Release Planning. Early, on purpose, and it will be a mess, also on purpose.
plain: The twenty-third. The first Release Planning session. It is early, deliberately, and it will be untidy, also deliberately.

natural: The gate closes behind them at fourteen forty. The phase boundary is a line in a document; everybody in the room will spend a year pretending it is a wall, which is the point of it.
plain: The gate review ends at 14:40. The boundary between phases is only a line in a document. Everyone in the room will spend a year treating it as a wall, and that is exactly its purpose.

natural: The old training room has one long wall and a smell of whiteboard marker that predates everyone in it. Deming has taped twelve printed lines to the wall at eye height. Someone has added a thirteenth in marker.
plain: The old training room has one long wall and smells of whiteboard marker. Deming has taped twelve printed lines to the wall at eye level. Somebody has added a thirteenth line in marker.

natural: The thirteenth is mine. Nobody reads the wall.
plain: The thirteenth line is mine. It says: nobody reads the wall.

natural: Then take it down and argue with the other twelve instead. I would rather be contradicted than decorative.
plain: Then take it down and argue with the other twelve instead. I would rather be contradicted than used as decoration.

natural: Fine. Risk want a stress view in Release 1. One scenario. The one they run every quarter and paste into tab nine.
plain: All right. The Risk division want a stress view in Release 1. One scenario. The one they run every quarter and copy into tab nine.

natural: I would rather build the engine. Anything Risk can write as a formula, the portal runs. Three iterations, maybe four with the tests.
plain: I would rather build the engine. Any formula that Risk can write, the portal can run. That is three iterations, maybe four including the tests.

natural: They asked for one scenario.
plain: They asked for one scenario.

natural: They will ask for more. They always ask for more.
plain: They will ask for more. They always ask for more.

natural: What problem is the engine solving?
plain: What problem does the engine solve?

natural: The next four requests.
plain: It solves the next four requests.

natural: Which nobody has made.
plain: Requests that nobody has made yet.

natural: Albert, in eleven months I will be building it anyway, badly, on top of something that assumed one scenario.
plain: Albert, in eleven months I will build it anyway. I will build it badly, on top of something that assumed there was only one scenario.

natural: Line nine. Simplicity, the art of maximising the amount of work not done. It is the only one of the twelve that costs you something to obey.
plain: Line nine on the wall. Simplicity: the art of maximising the amount of work that is not done. It is the only one of the twelve that costs you something to follow.

natural: Then say the same to me. If I build the data model for one scenario I will rebuild it in September, and rebuilding a model is not a bug fix, it is a summer.
plain: Then say the same thing to me. If I build the data model for one scenario, I will rebuild it in September. Rebuilding a model is not a small fix. It takes a whole summer.

natural: Charles. How long is the whole model, properly?
plain: Charles. How long does the complete model take, done properly?

natural: Ten weeks. Twelve if Finance change the maturity buckets again.
plain: Ten weeks. Twelve if the Finance division changes the maturity buckets again.

natural: And the part Release 1 actually needs?
plain: And the part that Release 1 actually needs?

natural: ...Eleven days.
plain: About eleven days.

natural: Then we will have this conversation eleven days from now, with something running.
plain: Then we will have this discussion again in eleven days, with something already working.

natural: Line one is mine and I am going to use it. Early and continuous delivery of something valuable. The Board Secretariat sees a page in March or everything I said to Lorenzo was decoration.
plain: Line one is mine and I will use it. Early and continuous delivery of something valuable. The Board Secretariat must see a page in March, or everything I told Lorenzo was decoration.

natural: Line twelve is the one nobody quotes and the one that will hurt us. Enterprise-aware. Brandeis exists. Turing exists. The Architecture Office exists and it is not an obstacle, it is where we work.
plain: Line twelve is the one nobody quotes, and the one that will cause us trouble. Be enterprise-aware. Brandeis exists. Turing exists. The Architecture Office exists. It is not an obstacle. It is where we work.

natural: As agile as needed, and as agile as possible, within the constraints of the organisation. I have that sentence pinned above my desk and I still cannot decide whether it is wisdom or an apology.
plain: Be as agile as needed, and as agile as possible, within the limits of the organisation. That sentence is pinned above my desk. I still cannot decide whether it is wisdom or an excuse.

natural: It reads like a licence to be neither.
plain: It reads like permission to be neither of those things.

natural: It reads like a description of where you work, Hedy.
plain: It reads like a description of the place where you work, Hedy.

natural: Line ten. At regular intervals the team reflects and adjusts. I want that from iteration one, not from iteration six when it is a rescue.
plain: Line ten. At regular intervals the team reflects and adjusts. I want that from iteration one, not from iteration six when it has become a rescue operation.

natural: Hedy. Three iterations of engine, or one iteration of the view Risk asked for. Marie prioritises, but you have the argument and I want it made properly.
plain: Hedy. Three iterations to build the engine, or one iteration to build the view that Risk asked for. Marie sets the priority, but the argument is yours and I want it made properly.

natural: One view. And when they ask twice I am going to say so out loud, and then generalise it in an afternoon, which will annoy me more than it annoys you.
plain: One view, then. And when they ask a second time I will say so out loud. Then I will make it general in one afternoon, which will annoy me more than it annoys you.

natural: Four times what? You have one request. The other three are Hedy's forecast of Risk, and Risk cannot forecast Risk.
plain: Four times what? You have one request. The other three are Hedy's prediction of what Risk wants, and Risk cannot predict that themselves.

natural: They will write down the four they can imagine this morning. In February there will be a fifth and it will be the important one.
plain: They will write down the four scenarios they can imagine this morning. In February there will be a fifth one, and it will be the important one.

natural: That is not delegation, that is a queue. In January they will pull whichever is at the top, and whichever is at the top is Marie's decision, and Marie is standing right here.
plain: That is not delegation. That is a waiting queue. In January they will take whichever item is at the top. Which item is at the top is Marie's decision, and Marie is standing here.

natural: The CASTOR Project Handbook is on Gantt's shelf. Ninety-four pages, and the spine is cracked in exactly one place, at change management.
plain: The CASTOR Project Handbook is on Gantt's shelf. It has 94 pages. The spine is broken in exactly one place, at the change management section.

natural: Two documents or one.
plain: Two documents, or one?

natural: One configuration item either way. I am not versioning two things that will contradict each other by March.
plain: It will be one configuration item either way. I will not version two documents that will contradict each other by March.

natural: One. Annex D of the Project Handbook. The guide calls it a separate artefact and then says in the next sentence that it does not need a separate carrier.
plain: One document. Annex D of the Project Handbook. The guide calls it a separate artefact, and then says in the next sentence that it does not need to be a separate document.

natural: And who writes it? You are the Team Coordinator. He is the Project Manager.
plain: And who writes it? You are the Team Coordinator. He is the Project Manager.

natural: I write it. He is accountable for it. That row is printed in the guide as the worked example, which I found irritating and then useful.
plain: I write it. He is accountable for it. That row is printed in the guide as its worked example. I found that irritating, and then useful.

natural: Read me the first line of section two.
plain: Read me the first line of section two.

plain: Nobody speaks into the pause. Lovelace, who worked with Tesla for eighteen months, looks at the four boxes instead.

plain: He was not wrong about the drawings. He was wrong about the order. Those are two different mistakes, and only one of them is mine.

plain: Then give me a rule I can hold you to. I do not want this argument again in February and again in May.

plain: Three of your items in Release 1: the replica, the audit trail, and half of the access zone. The rest in June.

plain: Yesterday I drafted the maturity bucket rules with Finance. Today I will do the edge cases. I am still waiting for their sign-off, which was promised on Tuesday. My confidence is four.

plain: I finished the spike last night. The batch window moves at month end, and nobody told us, because it is nobody's job to tell us. Next I will do the drill-through contract. My confidence is three.

plain: I reviewed the enabler design. Today I will work with Charles on the sync. I have no blocker. My confidence is three, and it is three because of his two, not because of my own work.

plain: While everyone is here: the Steering Committee papers close on Monday and Lorenzo de' Medici wants a position on Release 2. Can I go around the room for one line each on what will be delivered by June?

plain: Ada.

plain: You can have it at 11:00. You can have it in writing. You can have my burndown chart. You can have an hour of my time. But not in this meeting.

natural: Four people, sixty to ninety seconds each, four questions, all four about this iteration's goal. The moment it answers your question instead of theirs it is a different meeting with the same chairs.

You still have a Business Case, a Charter, four gates and a Steering Committee, and I have nothing to do with any of them.

plain: I have stood in this meeting forty times and asked for nothing. If I can do that, so can you.

plain: You would also have received a wrong answer. If you ask me today what will be delivered in June, I will say the reconciliation panel, because I want that to be true.

natural: Charles and Albert, ten minutes, at the board, when we break. Hedy, if you want the batch owner's name it is in the spike note.
plain: Charles and Albert, ten minutes at the board when we finish. Hedy, if you want the name of the batch owner it is in the spike note.

plain: I will book room B4 for 09:45. It is my problem.

plain: Lovelace does not book the room. She never does. She names the meeting and stops there. The person with the blocker finds a room themselves.

plain: The stand-up lasted eight minutes and ten seconds. The team leaves. You are left with Lovelace, a board, and a question that is still due on Monday.

plain: And when Lorenzo asks why the Project Manager cannot answer a question about his own project, in the room where the work is discussed?

plain: Say that the four of them told each other the truth this morning at 09:30, and that is why your report is worth reading. That is not a slogan. That is the whole exchange.

natural: The yellow square in the corner of the board says batch window, Babbage, Einstein. Beside it, from Tuesday, one that says Finance sign-off, Eiffel. Nothing on the board says Release 2.

natural: Then you get a number that survives Monday. And you keep the one place where Charles says two out loud on day four instead of day nine.
plain: Then you get a number that will survive Monday. And you keep the one meeting where Charles says his confidence is two on day four, instead of day nine.

natural: Then I prepare for you, not for them. My sixty seconds becomes a defence, and I stop saying the word blocked, because blocked in front of you is a different word.
plain: Then I prepare my update for you, not for them. My sixty seconds becomes a defence. I stop using the word blocked, because saying blocked in front of you means something different.

natural: Then three of us stand here for forty minutes while two of us talk. That is why the note has two names on it and not five.
plain: Then three of us stand here for forty minutes while two people talk. That is why the note has two names on it and not five.

natural: You would be the fifth speaker and the only one who is not building anything. Ada would spend her fifteen minutes protecting the first four from the last one.
plain: You would become the fifth speaker, and the only one who is not building anything. Ada would spend her fifteen minutes protecting the first four speakers from the last one.

plain: The meet after lasts eleven minutes. It ends with a name, a telephone number in the Infrastructure team, and an agreement that Babbage will telephone them himself.

natural: Behind them the build wall: a green strip, a red strip, and a counter that says three since the third of April.
plain: Behind them is the build wall. There is a green strip, a red strip, and a counter showing three broken builds since 3 April.

plain: Two of those three broken builds were mine, and both were caused by the reconciliation test fixtures. I merged at 16:30, the build went red at 17:30, and it was green again by 18:00.

natural: Which is the system working. I would rather see three reds in an iteration than one in September when eleven people are inside the same module.
plain: That is the system working correctly. I would rather see three broken builds in one iteration than one in September, when eleven people are working inside the same module.

natural: The reconciliation tests were written on the Tuesday before the code. Nine of them failed for two days on purpose. That is the part my own company still argues about.
plain: The reconciliation tests were written on the Tuesday, before the code. Nine of them failed for two days on purpose. That is the part my own company still argues about.

natural: The full suite runs at two in the morning against the replica. Four hundred and ten scenarios. Nothing goes to pre-production on a red suite and that is not my rule, it is in the plan.
plain: The full regression suite runs at 02:00 against the replica. There are 410 scenarios. Nothing goes to pre-production if the suite is red. That is not my personal rule; it is written in the Test Plan.

natural: Whose plan? Deming asked me that in December and I have been asked it twice since.
plain: Whose plan is it? Deming asked me that in December, and I have been asked the same question twice since then.

plain: It is mine. I drafted it, Albert argued about the integration scope, Marie confirmed what acceptance means, and your name is on it as the person who is Accountable for it.

natural: And the Finance control file is version four. Four, because they changed the maturity boundaries in February and did not think it was a change.
plain: And the Finance control file is at version four. Version four, because they changed the maturity boundaries in February and did not think that was a change.

natural: Every rule set is an item with a version and an owner now. Which copy is current, who changed it, when. Two years of Internal Audit answered by a repository nobody has to remember to use.
plain: Every rule set is now an item with a version and an owner. Which copy is current, who changed it, and when. Two years of Internal Audit questions are answered by a repository that nobody has to remember to use.

natural: Brandeis comes in without knocking, because the door was open, and stands in front of the wall reading it for a while before he says anything.
plain: Brandeis comes in without knocking, because the door was open. He stands in front of the wall and reads it for a while before speaking.

natural: One-two-seven. The drill-through. When a Risk analyst clicks a figure and reaches the source record, what is on that record?
plain: WIL-127, the drill-through. When a Risk analyst clicks on a figure and reaches the source record, what is on that record?

plain: The position, the instrument, the value date, the source system, and the last amendment.

plain: Nobody speaks for a moment. Einstein reaches past Lamarr and scrolls the record. There it is, third from the bottom: a staff user identifier and a time stamp.

natural: In September a supervisor in Vilnius sees that. Which is a person, identifiable, crossing to a third party. It may be perfectly lawful. It is not lawful because you assumed it.
plain: In September, a supervisor in Vilnius will see that. That is an identifiable person, and the data crosses to a third party. It may be perfectly lawful. But it is not lawful just because you assumed it was.

natural: It is in the Definition of Done. Line seven, Annex D. Screening by the Data Protection Coordinator for any item that exposes a source record.
plain: It is already in the Definition of Done. Line seven of Annex D. Screening by the Data Protection Coordinator for any item that exposes a source record.

natural: Then show me where it runs.
plain: Then show me where that screening runs.

natural: Lamarr brings up the pipeline. Unit tests, coverage, static analysis, integration, the nightly suite. Nine gates, green all the way down. Line seven of Annex D is not among them and neither is line eight.
plain: Lamarr opens the pipeline. Unit tests, coverage, static analysis, integration, and the nightly suite. Nine gates, all green. Line seven of Annex D is not one of them, and neither is line eight.

natural: Seven and eight are manual. Your screening and the accessibility check. They are on the checklist.
plain: Lines seven and eight are manual steps: your screening and the accessibility check. They are on the checklist.

natural: A checklist is not a gate. A gate stops something. Who does it? Not which team. Which chair.
plain: A checklist is not a gate. A gate stops something. Who performs it? Not which team. Which person.

natural: Four builders, an architect and a coordinator look at a wall of nine green lights, and none of them says a name.
plain: Four builders, an architect and a coordinator look at a wall showing nine green lights. None of them names a person.

natural: In my contract, done has eleven conditions and a signature. Here it has nine that a machine checks and two that a good mood checks.
plain: In my contract, done has eleven conditions and a signature. Here it has nine conditions that a machine checks and two that depend on someone's good mood.

natural: Noted, and I mean noted. It is not a planning question and it is not his question, it is ours. Bring it to the thirteenth, in the afternoon, with the data.
plain: Noted, and I mean properly noted. This is not a planning question and it is not his question. It is ours. Bring it to the retrospective on 13 April, in the afternoon, with the data.

plain: The 13th is acceptable. The item is released on 28 June, and I would rather be early and annoying than late and right.

plain: Last Wednesday afternoon, in this room, Hopper put a note from the Board Secretariat on the table. Curie rewrote four work items over two hours, while two analysts from Lending Operations argued about what a single page means.

plain: Two items were added, one was removed and four were rewritten. Today the team sees them for the first time. Tomorrow, for one hour, they are put into priority order.

natural: Three sessions, three rooms, three sets of people. Wednesday was Marie and Grace. Today is Marie and you. Tomorrow is Marie and Grace again with Albert on the enablers.
plain: There are three sessions, in three rooms, with three different groups. Wednesday was Marie and Grace. Today is Marie and the team. Tomorrow is Marie and Grace again, with Albert present for the enabler items.

natural: Every iteration, this. Twenty-six times over the project.
plain: This happens every iteration. That is twenty-six times over the project.

plain: At least once every iteration. When we scope national-authority access in the summer it will be weekly, because that subject will not stay stable for two weeks.

plain: You all received the six items on Friday. If you have not read them, say so now. I will read them out slowly, and we will lose forty minutes.

plain: Nobody says they have not read them. Babbage has printed his copy, which is his way of making the point twice.

plain: The reconciliation panel. As written in February, the panel shows each figure against the accounts and marks every difference. What has changed is Finance. Their control file comes quarterly, and I have been asking for a monthly one since January.

plain: So the acceptance criteria now include the case where the file is missing. What the panel shows, what it does not claim, and what the Risk division may conclude from it.

plain: These are points, not days. Nobody should take that thirty-four out of the room and call it five weeks.

plain: There are three more items. The access filter, the audit trail on the drill-through, and moving the sync outside the batch window. None of them appear on a screen, and all three are needed for June.

plain: Say the third one again in a sentence that Grace can repeat tomorrow. Tomorrow she will be arguing for something else, and I need to be able to explain why this came first.

plain: If the sync stays inside a batch window we do not control, then twice a quarter the portal shows wrong figures with confidence, and nobody discovers it until Finance reconciles.

plain: And the self-service report builder for December is still only one sentence in that list.

plain: It stays one sentence until somebody has designed it. I will not spend your Monday morning estimating something that will be rewritten twice before October.

plain: Six items were discussed, five were estimated, and one goes back to Marie because a rule is missing. The output of this meeting belongs to the team, not to her. She explained; you gave the sizes; you are answerable for them.

natural: And I read the outcome. I do not attend the argument.
plain: And I am told the outcome. I do not take part in the discussion.

plain: The meeting is one hour. The list is on the wall screen with the top thirty items in bold. Two user representatives sit at the end of the table. They have attended every one of these sessions since January.

natural: The scenario overlay goes into Release 2.
plain: The scenario overlay must go into Release 2.

natural: No.
plain: No.

plain: Marie, the Risk division has asked in three reviews in a row. Florence meets the Governors on 19 June and will be asked what happens to the figures under stress. I would like to give her an answer other than September.

natural: So would I. The panel goes first.
plain: So would I. The reconciliation panel goes first.

natural: Give me the reason and not the ranking.
plain: Give me the reason, not just the ranking.

plain: There are two open audit findings, both about whether the figures can be tied to the accounts. Until the panel exists, every scenario we show is a stress test on a figure nobody has reconciled. Risk would get a beautiful graph of a number I cannot defend.

natural: Hopper does not answer immediately, which in Hopper means the argument has landed and she is looking for a way to keep both things.
plain: Hopper does not answer at once. With Hopper, that means the argument has worked and she is looking for a way to keep both things.

plain: Then I will say it plainly. I am the Business Manager. She works for the business. If the business says the overlay is what June needs, what authority does the list have to say no?

natural: On yours. You gave it to her in November and it is written down.
plain: On your authority. You gave it to her in November, and it is written down.

plain: You support the priority, Grace. You do not set it. If you set it, then two people are ordering one list, and the team follows whichever of us spoke to them most recently.

natural: And if the two of you could not agree at all, then Grace and I step in. That is the mechanism and it exists. It is not for use on a Tuesday when one of you has a better argument than the other.
plain: And if you two could not agree at all, then Grace and I would step in. That mechanism exists. It is not for use on a Tuesday when one of you simply has the better argument.

natural: There is a version of this where you both get what you want and it costs Release 2 eight points.
plain: There is a version of this where you both get what you want, and it costs Release 2 eight points.

natural: Go on.
plain: Please continue.

plain: The overlay is a screen built on top of a calculation service that does not exist. Build that service in Release 2 as an enabler item. It shows nothing at all, Grace. But it means Release 3 can deliver the overlay in its first iteration instead of its third.

natural: So in June I tell the Governors the machinery is built and the screen comes in July.
plain: So in June I tell the Governors that the machinery is built and the screen arrives in July.

natural: In June you tell them it is built, because it will be, and I will demonstrate it to Marie from a log file with no screen at all, and she will accept it or she will not.
plain: In June you tell them it is built, because it will be. I will demonstrate it to Marie from a log file, with no screen at all, and she will either accept it or she will not.

natural: Panel first, service second, one-two-one stays where it is, overlay in Release 3. Grace, do you support that list.
plain: The panel first, the calculation service second, WIL-121 stays where it is, and the overlay stays in Release 3. Grace, do you support that list?

plain: I support that list. I object to the date, and I want that recorded in the minutes. In June somebody will ask me why the overlay was not delivered, and I want to have said this on the record.

plain: Release Plan version six goes out tonight to the whole Project Core Team. The velocity assumption drops from thirty-four to thirty, because six iterations of evidence is better than an assumption made in November.

plain: And because the contents of Release 2 have changed, it goes to the Steering Committee with two paragraphs from me. Not to approve Marie's ranking, but because what they were promised in June is now a different set of things.

natural: Two years ago I would have won that argument in the corridor afterwards.
plain: Two years ago I would have won that argument in the corridor afterwards.

plain: Two years ago you would have won it. Then Ada would have had two lists, and the second one would have been the real one.

plain: Yes. Send me the sentence about the sync, Marie. The one Albert made you learn. I meet Florence on Thursday.

plain: Then I have one list tonight and I can plan Monday's work against it. Grace's objection is in the minutes, and the enabler is in Release 2, which is more than she arrived with.

plain: You are Accountable for the plan. The order of items inside it is the one thing I do that nobody else can do. Take that away and I am a well-informed spectator with a job title.

plain: Then the next time Risk telephones me directly, I move it again. Ada plans two weeks of work against a list I changed on Wednesday without telling her. I have seen a project run that way. I do not want to be in another one.

plain: Then Lorenzo decides in ten days. Ada plans Monday's work against a list that may not survive. And the two people who understand the audit findings are in this room, not on that committee.

plain: It is the last day of the iteration. Two hours are booked, from 10:00 to 12:00. Eleven people are present, two of them user representatives from Lending Operations. Everyone has a laptop open, because today they will use the system themselves.
